start.speaker: Clerk
start.text: You're not on the visitor log. I didn't buzz anyone in. Please — whatever you're here for, I file things. That's all. I file things.

choices.text: The Reclamation Board. Who are they?
I need everything on the harbor districts.
Someone told you to lose a file. Who?

board.speaker: Clerk
board.text: The Board? Nobody, and everybody. Appointees. No elections, no names on the door. When a district stops turning a profit, they vote to 'reclaim' it — rezone it, run it down, let it go quiet. They don't hate anyone. That's the awful part. It's just accounting.

discover.title: The Reclamation Board
discover.desc: An unelected municipal body that 'reclaims' districts deemed unprofitable — rezoning them for managed decline. No malice, no names. Just a vote and a stamp. The clerk says the harbor came through like any other line item.

harbor.speaker: Clerk
harbor.text: The harbor... that order got walked in personally. Stamped same-day, which never happens. I was told to shelf it deep and forget the number. It's still here — third bank of cabinets, misfiled under Sanitation. I never touched it. You understand? I never touched it.

buried.speaker: Clerk
buried.text: A man from the tower. Polite. He didn't threaten me — he just mentioned my transfer had been 'approved, pending cooperation.' Thirty years I've kept this archive. They can erase me from it with one form. So I shelved the order and I stopped sleeping. That's the whole of my courage, detective. I'm sorry.

bye.speaker: Clerk
bye.text: Take what you came for. Just... put the drawers back the way you found them. It's all I can control now.
